articles.subject: codex-roster-lifecycle-and-scoped-successor-closure
articles.rule: CODEX-RECORD:The historical provision_type=sovereign record for codex is retired as a compatibility artifact and has no effective-sovereign state. Current Codex authority continues exclusively through the rule-declaration layer and A377;retiring the malformed roster record does not retire the Codex. XINGCHENG-ROSTER:the current 星澄 record rank is own-domain-sovereign-local-native-model-independent-privileged-domain under A378;this grants only enumerated 星澄-domain powers and does not make it a top decision/runtime/synchronization/permission sovereign. ACTIVE-ROSTER canonical IDs are decision-sovereign,system-runtime-sovereign,automation-sovereign,permission-sovereign and 星澄,with sub-sovereigns separately listed under parents;aliases cannot replace these IDs. LIFECYCLE:lineage and lifecycle use the same terminal meaning. A provision displaced by a known successor is superseded in both registries;retired means withdrawn without an operative successor;abolished is represented as retired plus explicit transfer/termination evidence and no effective record. EFFECTIVITY:active requires one effective record;non-active requires none. SCOPED-SUCCESSION:a predecessor may have multiple later provisions only when each successor declares a distinct non-overlapping subject/scope and the registry records that scoped relationship;within one conflict scope exactly one current successor is permitted. Multiple complementary successors such as native physical tree,ABI path and namespace dependency do not form competing authority. Ambiguous overlapping successors remain unresolved and cannot be silently selected by position/date. CONSISTENCY:every amendment verifies canonical IDs,roster type,lifecycle/effective parity,successor scope and metadata aliases. Pending directory implementation,external signatures,human signature and Language Governance FREEZE-PENDING remain pending until their own evidence passes and are not altered by this normalization.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:Codex compatibility row counted active+retiring Codex rule authority with its malformed sovereign row+星澄 treated as top general sovereign+runtime-sovereign alias published as canonical ID+lineage superseded/lifecycle retired mismatch+non-active effective record+overlapping active successors in one scope+automatic choice among ambiguous successors+normalization falsely closing pending implementation/signature/freeze gates.
articles.exception: Historical displays may retain old names/status text when explicitly marked historical and excluded from active/effective queries. Complementary scoped successors may coexist when their scopes and precedence are machine-verifiable.

articles.subject: non-disruptive-codex-amendment-ordinance-flow
articles.rule: PURPOSE:a Codex amendment must not interrupt,stop,restart,disconnect,reconfigure or partially mutate the running system. Every amendment follows this ordinance flow:1 RECEIVE explicit human/user amendment command and immutable amendment_id;2 SNAPSHOT current active Codex generation,history head,seals,read-only attributes and runtime reader generation;3 STAGE all proposed rows and Chinese confidential representation in an isolated non-authoritative transaction/generation;4 NORMALIZE identity,law classification,lineage,lifecycle,effective records,directories,test flows,metadata and version 1.00000 evolution rules;5 VALIDATE SQLite integrity,foreign keys,history/hash chain,seal roots,known references,unique scoped successors,authority/lifecycle/effective parity,confidentiality,mirror parity and applicable tests/audit;6 CERTIFY required evidence without fabricating external or human signatures;7 PREPARE immutable successor and generation manifest with rollback pointer to prior snapshot;8 ATOMIC-PUBLISH the complete generation by one generation-fenced pointer/transaction;9 NOTIFY consumers through typed shared-layer contract;10 RELOAD policy views only at safe boundaries using snapshot isolation;11 VERIFY old in-flight readers finish on prior generation,new readers use the published generation,system health/channel continuity remain intact;12 AUDIT result and restore read-only protection. Runtime services continue with the last fully accepted generation throughout staging/validation. No service may observe half-written Codex state. Publication does not itself execute newly declared implementation obligations,repair/update code,change permissions or restart a backend;those proceed through their own authorized ordinance and user-confirmation gates. If any step fails,the staged generation is rejected/quarantined,the active pointer remains unchanged,running service continues,and evidence is emitted. Concurrent amendments serialize by amendment lock and rebase/revalidate against the actual current history head;no lost update. Consumer incompatibility yields INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE or rejection,never forced reload. Emergency rollback is pointer restoration only to a previously sealed accepted generation and cannot erase the failed attempt or history.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:editing active generation in place+partial table/mirror publication+runtime restart or channel disconnect caused only by Codex update+new rule auto-executing implementation+publication before validation+fabricated signature+reader seeing mixed generations+concurrent lost amendment+failed staging replacing active snapshot+rollback by reset/overwrite/history deletion+Codex watcher triggering recursive repair/update.
articles.exception: A new rule may explicitly require a later controlled system restart for its own implementation, but the Codex amendment transaction itself remains non-disruptive and only records that pending obligation. A security-critical rule may block new unsafe operations after atomic publication while existing safe in-flight operations drain.

articles.subject: codex-readonly-state-review-isolation
articles.rule: Codex filesystem read-only state is a Codex protection control,not a prerequisite for inspecting or auditing unrelated system/runtime/module health. If a Codex artifact is unexpectedly writable,the reviewer records CODEX_PROTECTION_DEGRADED,verifies content hash/history/seal and isolates Codex mutation/publication;the condition does not stop,fail,skip or contaminate independent system review and does not make the running system unhealthy by itself. System review must continue and report its own findings. Writable state never grants amendment authority and never makes changed content effective. After an authorized amendment transaction,read-only protection is restored and separately verified. If content integrity also changed without authority,the last sealed generation remains authoritative while the incident is isolated and audited;unaffected runtime continues.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:using writable attribute alone to abort unrelated system review+reporting whole system failed solely because Codex is writable+trusting writable content as effective+silently ignoring writable state+automatic reset/overwrite to repair attributes+mixing Codex-protection finding into unrelated module verdict.
articles.exception: A review specifically scoped to Codex protection may fail or block Codex publication on writable state;that scoped verdict still cannot replace the independent system review result.

articles.subject: test-management-roster-and-historical-correction-closure

articles.subject: dynamic-test-management-roster-and-closure-status-successor
articles.rule: TEST-OWNERSHIP:owner=permission-sovereign in test_flow_directory and test_suite_architecture_directory means directory identity,schema,access and lifecycle authority only. health-maintenance-test-sub-sovereign is centralized management_owner for one-module-one-suite inventory,planning,scheduling,fixtures,execution coordination,evidence collection,retest and status reporting;it has no policy decision or direct module execution power and dispatches governed module test executors. articles.subject: dynamic-governance-code-resolution-and-hardcoding-elimination
articles.rule: DEFAULT:DYNAMIC-FIRST. Every value that may vary by machine,environment,worktree,module,generation,release,capacity or deployment is referenced by a registered governed code resolved through the owning canonical registry at the point of use. This includes physical paths,executables,ports/endpoints,credentials/secret references,model artifact locations,collection aliases,database DSNs,worktree locations,branch/remotes,tool IDs,module IDs,resource IDs,feature flags,timeouts,retry/pool/query budgets,capacity thresholds,versions and current counts/status. Implementations consume codes or typed configuration contracts and cannot duplicate resolved literal values. CODE-FORM:stable semantic code>registry record>environment/deployment binding>validated resolved value;records include code,owner,scope,type,schema/version,status,generation,source,default policy,validation,confidentiality and lineage. Environment variables carry codes or non-secret deployment bindings and never become authority. RESOLUTION:unknown,ambiguous,wrong-owner,stale,invalid-type,out-of-boundary or conflicting code fails closed with typed evidence;no silent guessed path,home-relative fallback or alternate hardcoded path. CACHE:resolved values are generation/version scoped and invalidated when registry/config/policy changes;cache is derived only. PRECEDENCE:Codex invariant>canonical registry>approved deployment binding>explicit one-time user command. NORMATIVE-LITERALS:a literal may remain in Codex only when it is itself the deliberately fixed normative identity/invariant,including version 1.00000,six governed languages,enumerated state machines,approved top-level root identities,public ABI identity and explicit security prohibition. Such a declaration does not authorize implementations to scatter the literal;they still resolve the registered code. Historical text remains immutable and is interpreted through current code mappings. MIGRATION:hardcoded implementation values are inventory findings,assigned an owning code,migrated consumer-by-consumer with compatibility evidence,and removed after zero-reference proof. Generated/third-party files are classified separately and cannot create an exception.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:runtime physical path/port/DSN/model/branch/timeout/count copied across modules+environment variable treated as authority+secret literal in Codex/config/source+unknown code falling back to guessed value+duplicate registries+cache surviving generation change+dynamic resolution changing authority+rewriting historical provisions to remove literals+calling a mutable deployment value a normative invariant.
articles.exception: A bootstrapping locator may contain the minimum fixed GPTBridge root identity needed to open the permission-owned registry,provided its exact scope is declared by the top-level-path special law and every subordinate value resolves dynamically. Isolated tests may use fixture literals that cannot escape the test boundary.

articles.subject: codex-canonical-reference-code-only-policy
articles.rule: CODEX-REFERENCE:current and future Codex provisions reference mutable/deployable entities by canonical code,not repeated physical or environment-specific values. DIRECTORY-FIRST:when an entity or physical value already exists in any permission-sovereign managed directory,the Codex and every subordinate/special law must reference that directory_code plus typed field selector;it cannot restate the resolved physical value. Resolution is dynamic against the current accepted directory generation. The minimum core code vocabulary is ROOT_GPTBRIDGE,DIR_MAIN_SYSTEM,DIR_STANDALONE_TOOLS,DIR_MODEL_DIALOGUE,DIR_XINGCHENG,DIR_SHARED_LAYER,STORE_POSTGRESQL_CENTRAL,STORE_SQLITE_MODULE,STORE_QDRANT_SEMANTIC,COLLECTION_SHARED_KNOWLEDGE,MODEL_EMBEDDING_CANONICAL,MODEL_RERANKER_CANONICAL,GIT_MAIN_BRANCH,GIT_REMOTE_CENTRAL,GIT_REMOTE_ORIGIN,POOL_WORKTREE_PERSISTENT,POOL_WORKTREE_EPHEMERAL,CHANNEL_INFORMATION_CANONICAL and CONTRACT_SHARED_LAYER. Codes identify semantics;their physical values exist exactly once in the permission-sovereign canonical reference registry and are resolved under A386. A provision defining a code may state its normative semantic meaning,but operational paths,ports,versions,dimensions,chunk sizes,models,collection names,branch names and capacity values belong to typed registry fields. HISTORICAL-MIGRATION:historical immutable literals remain evidence. Each still-effective legacy provision with mutable literals receives a code-mapping record immediately and an immutable code-based successor before its next affected release or configuration change;no in-place rewrite. Until successor completion,the mapping controls resolution and the literal cannot be copied into new law or implementation. CODE-CITATION:law text uses CODE[identifier] and optional field selector;reports may render resolved values with registry revision/hash and label them derived. SECRET codes resolve only inside authorized secret providers and never reveal values in Codex. OWNER:permission-sovereign governs identity/access/lifecycle of reference codes;domain owner supplies semantic truth;neither consumer nor environment invents codes.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:new mutable literal in Codex+restating a physical value already present in a directory+same physical value repeated as authority+code mapped in multiple registries+consumer inventing alias+historical literal copied forward+resolved value treated as Codex text+secret value stored in Codex+code without owner/type/version/status+changing mapping without new generation and affected evidence.
articles.exception: Irreducible normative constants such as the Codex version identity and closed legal state enums may be stated literally at their single definition point and referenced by code elsewhere. A one-time user command may supply a scoped value without creating persistent law.

articles.subject: governed-environment-variable-binding-fallback
articles.rule: RESOLUTION-ORDER:1 Codex fixed invariant;2 permission-sovereign directory/reference code and typed field;3 approved governed environment variable for a mutable deployment value not already stored in a directory;4 explicit one-time user command for its exact scope. If a physical/entity value exists in a directory,consumers use CODE[directory_code].field and cannot duplicate it in an environment variable as a second authority. ENV-SCOPE:environment variables may provide machine/session/deployment-specific values such as feature activation,temporary endpoint binding,process-local budget,toolchain discovery hint,non-persistent test fixture or secret-provider reference when no canonical directory field applies. Every allowed variable uses GPTBRIDGE_ prefix and has registry identity,owner,purpose,value type,required/optional status,validation/range,confidentiality,default policy,scope,consumer allowlist,generation and reload/restart semantics. AUTHORITY:environment is input/binding only,never Codex,directory,permission,data or identity authority. Its value cannot redefine owner,role,canonical ID,resource revision,law state or security boundary. VALIDATION:read once into a typed configuration snapshot at the governed boundary;reject unknown,malformed,out-of-range,conflicting,stale or unauthorized variables with a typed finding. No module reads arbitrary process environment throughout business logic. Optional absence uses an explicitly registered safe default or disabled state;no guessed path/port/model/credential. CHANGE:environment changes produce a new configuration generation and affected-scope validation;hot application follows update/reload law and cannot interrupt unrelated runtime. SECRET:prefer secret-provider references;when a secret value must enter through environment it is never persisted,echoed,logged,placed in evidence,child-process command line or inherited beyond the minimum allowlisted process. TESTS:fixture variables are isolated and cleared after test. EVIDENCE:record variable code,presence,source,generation,validation result and value hash/redaction,never confidential plaintext.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:environment duplicate of directory-owned physical value+environment treated as authority+unregistered variable+arbitrary os.environ/process.env reads in domain logic+secret logging/inheritance+silent coercion+unsafe implicit default+environment redefining identity/permission/law+change without generation invalidation+hardcoded fallback after missing variable.
articles.exception: The minimum bootstrap variable may locate CODE[ROOT_GPTBRIDGE] registry when the top-level-path law permits it;the resolved root must be validated and cannot broaden containment. CI/tests may inject registered fixture variables only inside isolated scope.

articles.subject: timestamp-only-hardcoding-invariant
articles.rule: ONLY-HARDCODE-ALLOWANCE:the only literal runtime/deployment value permitted to be hardcoded is a timestamp value created for an immutable event,revision,evidence or audit record. Every other value without exception is referenced through CODE[identifier].field or a registered governed environment variable under A387-A388. Paths,roots,filenames,ports,endpoints,hosts,branches,remotes,model names,dimensions,chunk sizes,collection/database/table names,language lists,state values,versions,IDs,owners,roles,timeouts,retries,budgets,limits,thresholds,feature flags and defaults cannot be duplicated as hardcoded literals in current law or implementation. Their single defining values live in typed canonical registries;even fixed legal enums and version identities receive codes and consumers reference the code. TIMESTAMP:hardcoded timestamp must be generated by the authoritative clock at event time,include timezone/UTC semantics and precision,be immutable after record creation and never be reused as configuration,deadline,timeout or identity. Historical literals remain immutable evidence but must be mapped to codes and cannot be copied forward. Source/checker scans classify authored literals,resolve exemptions only for typed timestamp fields and emit FAIL for every other hardcoded operational value.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:any non-timestamp hardcoded value+claiming a value fixed to evade code registration+timestamp used as configuration/default/timeout+manual fabricated event time+historical literal copied into successor+checker inventing literal whitelist+generated code hiding authored hardcode.
articles.exception: Test fixtures may contain isolated synthetic values only as fixture data declared by a registered fixture code;source still references the fixture code. Third-party/generated artifacts are evidence-classified and cannot supply authoritative configuration.

articles.subject: permission-sovereign-formal-audit-validation-authority
articles.rule: AUTHORITY:permission-sovereign is the sole formal owner of audit validation across the system. It defines and applies validation of audit identity,access scope,sequence,hash chain,signature,correlation,completeness,retention/rotation,confidentiality and admissibility against Codex-derived rules. It may return validated,rejected,incomplete,stale or conflict evidence and gate acceptance/release where audit proof is required. It has no module execution power and cannot rewrite/delete audit records,invent domain truth,repair code,approve its own unauthorized action or suppress a finding. COLLECTION:modules/shared-layer/synchronization executors append evidence through governed channels;they do not self-validate. XINGCHENG:星澄 retains independent inspection,correlation,challenge and finding capability under A378 but does not issue the formal permission-sovereign audit-validity verdict. Permission-sovereign cannot direct or suppress 星澄 findings;it validates their identity,scope,integrity and admissibility while domain truth remains with the domain owner. SEPARATION:validator identity is distinct from event actor,evidence collector and remediation executor. Validation decisions are themselves append-only audited and independently challengeable.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:module self-validating its audit+permission-sovereign executing repair/update+validator altering source evidence+星澄 formal verdict impersonation+permission validation suppressing independent finding+same actor producing and finally validating privileged evidence without separation+audit acceptance with broken hash/identity/scope/confidentiality.
articles.exception: A module may perform local pre-validation for fast feedback,marked non-authoritative;formal acceptance still requires permission-sovereign validation.

articles.subject: canonical-timestamp-envelope-fields
articles.rule: TIMESTAMP-ENVELOPE:every immutable event/evidence/audit/revision record uses the applicable formal fields occurred_at_utc,recorded_at_utc,observed_at_utc,effective_at_utc,expires_at_utc,source_clock_id,time_zone,utc_offset,precision,monotonic_sequence,clock_skew_ms,timestamp_status and timestamp_hash. occurred_at_utc is when the source event happened;recorded_at_utc is durable append time;observed_at_utc is measurement time;effective_at_utc is legal/config activation time;expires_at_utc is nullable only when non-expiry is legally declared. FIXED-FORMAT:every canonical UTC timestamp is exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ in Gregorian calendar,24-hour time,UTC,with six fractional-second digits and uppercase Z;canonical storage forbids omitted fractions,numeric offsets,spaces,locale month names and naive time. precision is fixed to microsecond. time_zone and utc_offset are separate display/source-evidence fields and never alter canonical UTC storage. source_clock_id references the registered clock;monotonic_sequence orders events when wall clock ties/regresses;clock_skew_ms records measured uncertainty;timestamp_status is verified|estimated|corrected|invalid;timestamp_hash binds the normalized envelope to its record. HARD-CODE:only concrete immutable values stored in these timestamp fields qualify for A389 allowance. Field names,format,zones,clock IDs,expiry policy and status vocabulary are referenced by schema codes rather than scattered literals. CORRECTION:timestamps are never overwritten;an error appends a corrected successor with original timestamp_hash,reason,authority and correlation_id. VALIDATION:permission-sovereign formally validates time evidence as part of audit validation;domain collectors supply source evidence. Missing required field,wrong fixed format,naive local time,impossible ordering,excess skew,unregistered clock or hash mismatch makes evidence incomplete/invalid without stopping unrelated system review.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:canonical timestamp outside YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ+ambiguous local time+missing required source zone evidence+recorded time substituted for occurrence without status+timestamp overwrite+clock regression hidden+timestamp literal outside formal field+timestamp used as configuration identity+unregistered clock+permission validator fabricating source time+invalid time failing unrelated system review.
articles.exception: Legacy records may retain their original format when paired with a canonical converted UTC timestamp and immutable migration evidence;the original is evidence only. A source unable to prove occurrence time uses estimated status and explicit uncertainty;it cannot claim verified.

articles.subject: xingcheng-codex-implementation-compliance-classification
articles.rule: MANDATE:CODE[INSTITUTION_XINGCHENG] inspects not only runtime faults but also whether CODE[CODEX_CURRENT_GENERATION] and governed implementation agree. Inspection scope includes declarations,authority/ownership,paths through directory codes,identities,contracts,API/ABI/schema,dependency direction,configuration codes,environment bindings,security,tests,evidence,lifecycle,release state and observable runtime behavior. INPUTS:use the current sealed/effective Codex generation,canonical registries,SourceIndex/GovernanceIR/LanguageGraph,current source/build/runtime evidence and affected-scope/full verification as applicable. Never compare against a stale report or superseded provision. METHOD:1 resolve current applicable provisions and codes;2 state the expected obligation and acceptance evidence;3 collect implementation declaration plus observed evidence;4 test contradiction,absence,ambiguity and feasibility;5 trace ownership and revision;6 classify;7 issue separate findings;8 submit audit evidence to CODE[ROLE_PERMISSION_SOVEREIGN] for formal validation. CLASSIFICATION:CODE[FINDING_IMPLEMENTATION_ISSUE] applies only when the Codex rule is current,internally coherent,applicable and testable but source/config/build/runtime/evidence violates or omits it. CODE[FINDING_CODEX_ISSUE] applies only when the governing rule itself is contradictory,ambiguous,missing required semantics,uses unresolved/duplicate codes,has invalid lineage/lifecycle/precedence,requires impossible evidence or conflicts with a higher/current provision. CODE[FINDING_INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE] applies when neither conclusion is provable;it cannot be reported as compliant. If one incident contains both,a single vague BOTH verdict is forbidden:emit two linked findings,one implementation issue and one Codex issue,each with its own evidence,owner and required action. OUTPUT:each finding includes finding_id,classification,rule/code references,implementation target,expected,observed,evidence hashes,source revision,CodeX generation,scope,severity,certainty,owner,impact,required action,retest condition,correlation_id and CODE[TIMESTAMP_FORMAT_CANONICAL] timestamps. ROUTING:implementation issue goes to its registered implementation owner and normal repair/change workflow;Codex issue goes to explicit user/human amendment workflow under CODE[CODEX_AMENDMENT_FLOW],never automatic source repair. CODE[INSTITUTION_XINGCHENG] may challenge,suggest and re-inspect but cannot formally validate its own audit evidence,change permission or silently amend Codex. EFFECT:no finding alone mutates code,Codex,registry or status. Critical mismatch isolates only unsafe affected scope;unaffected system review and runtime continue.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:fault-only inspection+assuming implementation wrong whenever mismatch exists+assuming Codex wrong to excuse implementation+vague combined verdict+classification without current rule and observed evidence+stale/superseded comparison+automatic Codex rewrite+CODE[INSTITUTION_XINGCHENG] self-validating formal audit+finding directly executing repair+missing owner/retest/correlation+compliance PASS on incomplete evidence.
articles.exception: A fast save-time inspection may use affected-scope evidence and mark untouched scopes not-evaluated;integration/release or Codex-wide claims require full applicable verification. Emergency isolation may precede final classification but cannot predetermine it.

articles.subject: precise-coded-fault-and-compliance-detail-display
articles.rule: NO-VAGUE-FINDING:every fault,implementation issue and Codex issue is displayed as a concrete individually addressable record;generic labels such as system error,unknown failure,compliance problem or something went wrong cannot be the final finding. IDENTITY:display CODE[FAULT_CODE] or CODE[COMPLIANCE_FINDING_CODE] plus CODE[CANONICAL_CODENAME],human title and classification. DETAIL:the required governed detail schema contains finding_id,incident_id,parent/root_cause_group,classification_code,fault_or_rule_code,canonical_codename,title,summary,full_detail,severity,certainty,status,source_revision,CodeX_generation,affected_module_code,owner_code,exact_file_code,resolved_file_path,repository_root_code,line_start,line_end,symbol_or_entry,artifact_or_process,contract_or_operation,rule/provision references,expected,observed,reproduction_or_detection_steps,root_cause,impact,affected_scope,isolation_state,proposed_action_code,action_detail,risk,rollback_or_fallback,retest_condition,evidence hashes,correlation_id and formal timestamps. FILE-PRECISION:implementation findings must resolve to the narrowest authored source/config/build/migration/test file responsible and include line range plus symbol/entry when parse evidence permits. Multiple responsible files are separate linked targets,not one directory-level accusation. Runtime/generated artifact faults identify the artifact/process and trace to its owning authored file or explicitly state which mapping evidence is missing under CODE[FINDING_INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE]. Codex issues identify exact provision_id/table/row/field or missing provision slot and the conflicting higher/current rule;CODEX database filename alone is insufficient. DISPLAY:single fault shows one full record;multiple faults show every record separately in deterministic severity,time,code order with total/unresolved counts. Collapsed summaries may accompany but never replace details. Paths are rendered from CODE[DIRECTORY_REFERENCE].field and are derived display values,not new hardcoding. REDACTION:secrets/personal/confidential Codex content is redacted by field policy while preserving code,location class,hash and actionable reason;redaction cannot make the finding vague. VALIDATION:CODE[ROLE_PERMISSION_SOVEREIGN] rejects any audit finding lacking required identity,exact target,expected/observed,evidence or retest fields.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:vague final error+missing code or codename+directory-only implementation target when file is knowable+missing line/symbol without parser reason+multiple files/faults collapsed into one target+Codex issue without exact provision/table/field+details replaced by summary+unknown used without enumerating missing evidence+hardcoded path instead of directory code+redaction hiding actionable classification+formal validation of incomplete detail.
articles.exception: When a crash prevents immediate file resolution,the preliminary record may use CODE[FINDING_INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE] with exact artifact/process,stack/evidence and missing mapping;it must be enriched before repair approval or final classification. Line numbers may be omitted for binary artifacts when symbol/build/source mapping is provided.

articles.subject: code-reference-and-hardcoding-separation-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A389 is superseded. GENERAL-RULE:operational values are resolved from typed canonical code registries or governed environment bindings and are not duplicated across law or implementation. SEPARATION:this article governs only literal/reference placement;it does not define timestamp representation or version-number semantics. Timestamp fields,format,clock evidence and correction are governed exclusively by A391. Version namespaces,format,authority,evolution and comparison are governed exclusively by A395 together with their cited version provisions. A timestamp value and a version number are distinct typed identities and neither may substitute for,derive from,or encode the other. DEFINITION:authoritative registry declarations,legal schema definitions,code identities and immutable evidence values are canonical definitions rather than duplicated operational hardcoding;their consumers still reference registered identities. CHECKING:a finding must name the literal,its semantic class,the expected registry/environment/timestamp/version authority and the exact file or Codex field.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:combining timestamp-format and version-format into one rule+timestamp used as version+version used as time+duplicated operational literal+checker treating canonical registry definition as consumer hardcoding+checker inventing exemptions+copying historical literal into a new operational consumer.
articles.exception: Test fixtures may use registered synthetic fixture data. Third-party/generated artifacts remain classified evidence and cannot become configuration authority.

articles.subject: canonical-version-number-contract
articles.rule: VERSION-ONLY:this article governs version numbers and never timestamp fields or clock evidence. NAMESPACES:Codex version,application version,tool version,release identity,contract version,schema version,ABI version,governance-schema version and runtime generation are typed non-interchangeable identities with one registered authority each. CODEX-FORMAT:the current Epoch 2 Codex version is the exact five-fractional-digit decimal identity 1.00000 until an explicit user amendment authorizes natural evolution;revision history may advance while this version remains unchanged. EVOLUTION:version changes follow the registered version-evolution policy and immutable successor history;automatic repair,automatic update,models,checkers and runtime processes cannot infer,bump,normalize,downgrade or rewrite a version. COMPARISON:compare only within the same namespace using its registered parser and authority;floating-point arithmetic,filesystem time,Git time,build time and event timestamps are never version authority. DISPLAY:a timestamp may accompany a version record only as separate metadata and cannot be embedded into or parsed as the version number.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:timestamp-derived version+version-derived timestamp+date-version substitution+cross-namespace comparison+floating-point version arithmetic+automatic bump/reset/downgrade+filename/path/mtime/Git/package/cache as version authority+silent normalization+combining version and timestamp fields.
articles.exception: A legacy externally defined semantic version may retain its native registered syntax inside its own namespace;it cannot redefine the Codex version format or be compared across namespaces.

articles.subject: automatic-repair-and-update-command-code-registration
articles.rule: REGISTRATION:automatic repair and automatic update use only the registered command codes XINGCHENG_SET_REPAIR_RELEASE,XINGCHENG_SET_UPDATE_RELEASE,SYNC_EXECUTE_APPROVED_AUTOMATIC_REPAIR and SYNC_EXECUTE_APPROVED_AUTOMATIC_UPDATE. CONTROL:the first two commands record the user's independent auxiliary-system switch choice and never execute mutation. EXECUTION:the latter two accept only a current one-time user confirmation bound to action identity,target,scope,method,risk,evidence digest,expiry and rollback/fallback under A366 and A380;dispatch remains through the governed synchronization execution chain. DISABLED/MISSING:disabled switch,missing confirmation,expired confirmation,identity mismatch or unregistered command fails closed without suppressing detection,diagnosis or isolated reporting. EVIDENCE:every request/result records command code,request identity,user actor,decision,correlation,formal timestamp and affected target;retry follows the command directory idempotency contract and cannot broaden scope.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:unregistered repair/update command+one command controlling both switches+switch command executing mutation+execution command without one-time user confirmation+model/system toggling user switch+alias bypass+confirmation reuse+scope expansion+command directory inventing implementation behavior.
articles.exception: A user may issue a separate explicit one-time manual repair or update command under the existing user-command exception;it does not enable either automatic switch or create standing authority.

articles.subject: canonical-timestamp-envelope-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A391 is superseded. TIMESTAMP-ONLY:this article governs timestamp fields,clock evidence,normalization and correction and never defines or evolves a version number. PROFILE:each immutable event,evidence,audit or revision record applies the registered timestamp profile for that record type. The minimum canonical envelope contains recorded_at_utc,source_clock_id,precision,timestamp_status and timestamp_hash;occurred_at_utc,observed_at_utc,effective_at_utc,expires_at_utc,time_zone,utc_offset,monotonic_sequence and clock_skew_ms are required when their declared semantics apply. FORMAT:canonical UTC values use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ,Gregorian calendar,24-hour UTC,six fractional digits and uppercase Z. STATUS:verified|estimated|corrected|invalid. SEPARATION:timestamp values are immutable evidence values allowed by A394;field/schema/status definitions are canonical declarations,not consumer hardcoding. A timestamp cannot act as a version,release identity,generation or ordering authority except that monotonic_sequence resolves equal/regressed wall-clock observations. LEGACY-MIGRATION:legacy timestamp rows retain the original value and append canonical_recorded_at_utc,timestamp_status and immutable migration evidence;date-only revision history is estimated at the declared UTC boundary and cannot claim occurrence precision. CORRECTION:never overwrite source evidence;append or store a paired canonical successor with reason,authority and correlation. VALIDATION:permission-sovereign validates timestamp evidence admissibility while 星澄 independently inspects Codex/implementation agreement.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:version rule inside timestamp article+timestamp as version+version as timestamp+naive canonical time+omitted six-digit fraction+numeric-offset canonical storage+invented occurrence precision+overwriting legacy source value+unregistered clock+hidden clock regression+invalid timestamp blocking unrelated scope.
articles.exception: A source that cannot prove occurrence time records estimated status and uncertainty. A non-expiring record may omit expires_at_utc only when its registered timestamp profile declares non-expiry.

articles.subject: automatic-repair-update-command-contract-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A396 is superseded. COMMAND-SET:the complete registered command chain is XINGCHENG_SET_REPAIR_RELEASE,XINGCHENG_SET_UPDATE_RELEASE,XINGCHENG_CONFIRM_AUTOMATIC_REPAIR,XINGCHENG_CONFIRM_AUTOMATIC_UPDATE,XINGCHENG_REVOKE_AUTOMATIC_REPAIR_CONFIRMATION,XINGCHENG_REVOKE_AUTOMATIC_UPDATE_CONFIRMATION,SYNC_EXECUTE_APPROVED_AUTOMATIC_REPAIR and SYNC_EXECUTE_APPROVED_AUTOMATIC_UPDATE. ROLE-SEPARATION:user owns switch choice,confirmation and revocation;星澄 auxiliary system presents controls and records the user's command without deciding for the user;permission-sovereign validates actor/action/target/scope and evidence admissibility;automation-sovereign owns update/repair synchronization decision and module assignment;module-execution layer alone performs mutation. CONTRACT-REGISTRATION:every command_code_directory row is its canonical command registration. Switch request fields are command_code,request_id,user_actor_id,desired_state,choice_revision,session_id,correlation_id,recorded_at_utc;confirmation request fields add action_id,category,target_code,scope_code,method_code,risk_code,evidence_digest,expires_at_utc,rollback_or_fallback_code;revocation request fields add confirmation_id and reason_code;execution request fields require confirmation_id,confirmation_hash,permission_proof,synchronization_decision_id,executor_id,expected_before_hash and generation. Every result contains command_code,request_id,decision,status,reason_code,correlation_id,recorded_at_utc and evidence_hash. VERSIONING:the request/result contract identity suffix is a contract version governed by A395 and is separate from its A397 timestamps. GATES:execution requires enabled matching switch plus current unrevoked single-use confirmation plus permission proof and synchronization decision. Missing/mismatched/expired/replayed input fails closed. No checker or executor creates an exception.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:unregistered alias+combined repair/update switch+implicit/preselected switch+confirmation embedded without registered confirmation command+missing revocation path+confirmation reuse+permission validator becoming executor+synchronization decision performing module work+module execution changing scope+contract fields inferred from timestamp/version+automatic contract repair.
articles.exception: An explicit one-time manual user command remains lawful but does not enable an automatic switch,create persistent consent or bypass permission and evidence validation.

articles.subject: timestamp-version-cross-codex-separation-interpretation
articles.rule: INTERPRETATION:A397 is the sole current timestamp representation rule and A395 is the sole current version-number rule. Earlier provisions including A182,A366 and A380 remain effective only for their domain duties;their words time,timestamp,expiry,version,generation or release reference the applicable typed authority and do not establish another format. A394 governs only value-reference placement. PRECEDENCE:on representation conflict A397 controls timestamps and A395 controls versions;neither controls the other's namespace. REFERENCES:new provisions,registries,commands and contracts cite the applicable article instead of restating formats. CHECKERS:emit separate findings for timestamp violation and version violation even when one record contains both.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:implicit mixed timestamp-version type+restated competing format+one finding concealing two violations+legacy wording overriding A397/A395+timestamp correction changing version+version evolution rewriting timestamp evidence.
articles.exception: A historical provision remains immutable evidence;this interpretation narrows only its current application and does not rewrite historical text.

articles.subject: whole-system-modular-architecture
articles.rule: MODULE:every owned area of the system is one independently identified module with exactly one module code,one identity group,one lifecycle and one failure boundary; IDENTITY:module code and identity group are unique,stable and never shared across modules; OWNERSHIP:each module owns its own state,resources,refresh and automation and never mutates another module's state directly; COMPOSITION:system behavior is the composition of module behaviors through governed interfaces only; DEPENDENCY:module dependencies are declared and acyclic; FAILURE:module failure is contained to that module and its declared dependents; NO-GLOBAL-STALL:no module may block,stall or crash the main system by construction.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:shared module code+shared identity group+two modules in one entity+implicit cross-module state mutation+module failure propagating beyond its boundary+one module blocking the main system
articles.exception: A governed shared service may serve several modules only when declared as its own module with its own code and identity group.

articles.subject: module-code-and-identity-group-itemization
articles.rule: PERMISSION-DIRECTORY:the permission directory is itemized to the module level; each module resolves exactly one module code and exactly one identity group; AUTHORIZATION:every request is evaluated against the requesting module's own code and identity group only; ISOLATION:a token or grant issued for one module's group can never be replayed as another module's identity; COVERAGE:every registered module has one enabled identity,one code and one group,with no orphan and no duplicate; CHANGE:additive-versioned registration only,retired codes remain reserved.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:module without own identity group+two modules sharing one identity group+code reuse across modules+group reuse across modules+unregistered module acting
articles.exception: Companion tools nested under an owner module share the owner's permission profile only when the codex explicitly declares them as companions.

articles.subject: modular-field-scoped-refresh-no-whole-ui-refresh
articles.rule: REFRESH-OWNER:the backend owns refresh; it evaluates state and pushes reports; CLIENTS:the frontend only renders reports it receives and never polls; SCOPE:frontend state is distributed per field to module subscribers; each module re-renders only when its own subscribed field changes; NO-WHOLE-REFRESH:whole-UI refresh,whole-page reload and monolithic state replacement are forbidden; REPORT:periodic reports are compact; the per-item surface is included when a fault or its resolution occurs so modules update immediately; BLOCKING:all projection and evaluation work runs off the event loop and off the UI critical path.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:whole-UI refresh+whole-page reload+client polling as the primary refresh path+monolithic state object driving all rendering+blocking evaluation on the event loop or UI path
articles.exception: A user-initiated explicit refresh of one module may fetch that module's full snapshot on demand.

articles.subject: module-fault-isolation-and-main-system-liveness
articles.rule: ISOLATION:every module executes behind its own boundary; a module error,timeout or failure is contained,reported and never propagates to other modules; LIVENESS:as long as operation is unaffected no module may stall the whole main system; NON-BLOCKING:all module work uses bounded timeouts and runs off shared critical paths; DEGRADATION:a failing module degrades or hides itself while the remaining modules continue; OBSERVABILITY:each module reports its own fault and resolution state separately; RECOVERY:module recovery is per-module and never requires stopping unaffected modules.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:module failure crashing the main system+module failure blocking another module+unbounded module operation+shared critical path monopolized by one module+recovery requiring whole-system stop
articles.exception: A verified security or integrity failure may isolate the affected module fail-closed while all unaffected modules continue.

articles.subject: modular-automation-and-automation-isolation
articles.rule: AUTOMATION:automatic update and automatic repair are modular;each automation unit is bound to its module code and identity group and acts only within that module's scope; ISOLATION:each automation unit runs independently with its own status,error and heartbeat; one unit's failure never disables or delays another unit or the main system; SCHEDULING:units are scheduled independently and bounded; DETECTION:detection,classification and evidence collection continue regardless of execution gates; EXECUTION:execution follows the module's switch and the user's per-item confirmation; OBSERVABILITY:per-unit automation state is reported separately.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:one automation unit governing all modules+unit failure disabling other units+unit failure stalling the main system+unbounded automation scheduling+automation acting outside its module scope
articles.exception: A governed cross-module maintenance action may be requested only through the owning module's declared interface and permission.

articles.subject: independent-tool-single-instance-entity
articles.rule: ENTITY:each independent tool is exactly one entity;one tool id,one runtime instance,one code and one identity group; START:starting an already-running tool activates or reports the existing instance instead of spawning a second; DUPLICATE:duplicate tool processes,duplicate windows and duplicate registrations are forbidden; ISOLATION:each tool runs in its own failure boundary and cannot block tools or the main system; LIFECYCLE:tool lifecycle is owned and recorded per tool with single-instance enforcement at spawn,registration and recovery.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:duplicate independent tool instance+two processes for one tool id+two identities for one tool+restart spawning a duplicate while an instance is alive
articles.exception: A bounded standby generation for governed release handover is one logical entity with a single active instance and is not a duplicate.

articles.subject: timestamp-derived-version-identity-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A395 is superseded. VERSION-IDENTITY:every new Codex,application,tool,release,contract,schema,ABI,governance-schema and runtime-generation version is a UTC timestamp identity formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. The registered issuing authority assigns it once at seal or activation;the value is immutable,unique within its namespace and ordered as UTC time. This replaces creation of new decimal or semantic numeric versions. SEPARATION:this article governs version identity only;A410 governs event/evidence timestamps. A version timestamp is not occurred_at_utc,recorded_at_utc or file modification time even when values coincide. COLLISION:multiple releases in one second append the registered monotonic sequence as a separate identity component;they do not fabricate time. LEGACY:1.00000 and earlier numeric values remain read-only aliases and lineage evidence only;they cannot select,order or activate current state. EXTERNAL:upstream dependency versions remain descriptive evidence and bind to a local timestamp version identity. AUTOMATION:no repair,update,model or checker may infer or rewrite a version from mtime,Git,build,filename or cache.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:new numeric version authority+semantic-version increment for GPTBridge identity+mtime/Git/build/cache-derived version+event timestamp silently reused as version+cross-namespace comparison+timestamp-version overwrite+legacy numeric alias selecting current state+fabricated collision time.
articles.exception: Legacy consumers may read preserved numeric aliases during migration but every newly issued identity and activation record uses the timestamp version.

articles.subject: timestamp-version-separation-interpretation-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A399 is superseded. INTERPRETATION:A406 exclusively defines timestamp-derived version identities;A410 exclusively defines event,evidence,audit and revision timestamp envelopes;A409 exclusively defines code and environment reference placement. Earlier provisions retain domain duties but establish no competing version or timestamp format. The word version in a current operational rule resolves to a typed A406 timestamp version unless explicitly marked legacy_version_alias. The word timestamp resolves to an A410 evidence field unless explicitly marked version_identity. CHECKERS:version identity misuse and evidence timestamp misuse are separate findings with exact table,field,file and expected authority.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:one untyped timestamp field serving both version and evidence+legacy text overriding current successor+mixed finding hiding two violations+event-time correction changing version identity+version activation rewriting event evidence.
articles.exception: Historical provisions and values remain immutable evidence;this successor changes only current interpretation.

articles.subject: automatic-command-contract-timestamp-version-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A398 is superseded. COMMAND-SET:the registered repair/update switch,confirmation,revocation and approved-execution commands remain exhaustive. CONTRACT-VERSION:each request and response contract has a canonical contract_version_identity issued under A406. Existing identifiers ending -v1 are legacy aliases only and resolve through command_contract_revision_registry;no new -v2 or numeric contract suffix is created. CONTRACT-RECORD:contract_id,legacy_alias,version_identity,request_schema,response_schema,owner,content_hash,status and predecessor_contract_id are mandatory. ROLE-SEPARATION:user decides switch/confirmation/revocation;星澄 presents and records;permission-sovereign validates permission and evidence;automation-sovereign decides synchronized dispatch;module execution alone mutates. GATE:enabled matching switch,current unrevoked single-use confirmation,permission proof,synchronization decision,before hash and generation are all required. Action/evidence timestamps use A410 fields separately from contract_version_identity.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:new numeric contract version+unregistered alias+implicit consent+confirmation reuse+missing revocation+permission execution+synchronization module work+executor scope expansion+contract version confused with action time.
articles.exception: Legacy -v1 aliases remain readable during bounded migration but cannot identify a newly issued contract.

articles.subject: dynamic-reference-policy-timestamp-version-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A394 is superseded. GENERAL:operational values are consumed through typed canonical codes or governed environment bindings. Canonical registry declarations,legal schema definitions,code identities,immutable A410 evidence timestamps and sealed A406 version identities are authoritative definitions rather than duplicated consumer hardcoding. SEPARATION:A406 defines version identity,A410 defines evidence timestamp,A409 defines only reference placement. Consumers never restate paths,endpoints,models,limits,states,contracts or identities. CHECKING:each finding names the literal,semantic class,expected authority and exact file or Codex field. Historical literals remain evidence and are not copied forward.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:duplicated operational literal+canonical definition treated as consumer hardcoding+invented whitelist+timestamp format restated outside A410+version semantics restated outside A406+legacy number used as current identity.
articles.exception: Registered fixtures and third-party/generated evidence remain bounded and non-authoritative.

articles.subject: canonical-evidence-timestamp-envelope-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A397 is superseded. EVIDENCE-TIMESTAMP:this article governs event,evidence,audit and revision times,not version identity. Canonical UTC fields use YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ffffffZ with six fractional digits and uppercase Z. Applicable profiles use occurred_at_utc,recorded_at_utc,observed_at_utc,effective_at_utc,expires_at_utc,source_clock_id,precision,timestamp_status,timestamp_hash,monotonic_sequence,clock_skew_ms,time_zone and utc_offset. STATUS:verified|estimated|corrected|invalid. VERSION-SEPARATION:version_identity is governed by A406 and stored in a different typed field;an evidence timestamp cannot activate or order versions. LEGACY:original values remain and canonical companions plus migration evidence are appended;estimated values never claim original precision. VALIDATION:permission-sovereign validates admissibility while 星澄 independently inspects compliance.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:evidence timestamp used as version+version identity used as occurrence time+missing fractional precision+naive canonical time+overwrite+fabricated precision+unregistered clock+hidden regression+invalid time blocking unrelated scope.
articles.exception: A record lacking provable occurrence time uses estimated status;non-expiry is allowed only through its registered profile.

articles.subject: timestamp-version-issuance-and-collision-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A406 is superseded. VERSION-IDENTITY:new GPTBridge Codex,application,tool,release,contract,schema,ABI,governance-schema and runtime-generation versions use authoritative UTC identities formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ. ISSUE:the registered sealing or activation authority issues exactly one version identity per namespace per UTC second and the new identity must be later than the prior active identity. If another candidate is ready inside the same second,it waits for the next authoritative clock second;monotonic_sequence remains separate evidence and is never appended to or encoded in the version. CHANGE-CLASS:change severity and compatibility class are separate registered fields and never encoded through numeric increments or timestamp manipulation. LEGACY:numeric and semantic versions remain immutable aliases or external dependency evidence only. SEPARATION:A410 governs evidence timestamp envelopes;the version identity is a distinct typed activation field even though it uses UTC syntax. SOURCE:file mtime,Git time,build time,cache time and observed event time are not issuing authorities.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:more than one version per namespace per second+composite version unsupported by parser+monotonic sequence embedded in version+new numeric increment+severity encoded in timestamp+fabricated future second+mtime/Git/build/cache-derived version+legacy alias selecting active state.
articles.exception: An upstream dependency may retain its external semantic version as descriptive evidence after binding to a local timestamp version identity.

articles.subject: timestamp-version-change-classification-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A100 and A109 are superseded for current operation. CLASSIFICATION:editorial,clarification,provision-scope,authority-duty,architecture-authority and complete-reconstitution remain change classes ordered by impact,not version increments. Each amendment records change_class_code,criterion,precedence,required review,compatibility effect and timestamp version identity. EVOLUTION:a valid successor has an A411 identity later than the current identity,immutable lineage,content hashes,certification and applicable signatures. No arithmetic is performed on a version and no change class adds a decimal amount. VALIDATION:the permission-sovereign validates identity and evidence;the human amendment authority decides the normative change;星澄 may inspect and challenge but cannot issue the identity. MIGRATION:version_evolution_rules numeric increments are historical evidence marked legacy-retired and timestamp_version_evolution_rules is the current registry.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:version addition+decimal increment+floating-point comparison+change severity inferred from timestamp distance+timestamp fabricated to encode class+legacy increment table used for current issuance+automatic classification changing law.
articles.exception: Historical revisions retain their original numeric versions and degrees;they are not recalculated.

articles.subject: timestamp-version-ledger-and-recovery-integrity
articles.rule: LEDGER:revision_history remains append-only across a version-format migration and cannot be cleared,restarted or replaced. A recovered row is marked corrected or estimated,identifies its source evidence and never claims verified status unless its original signed record is proven. VERSION-MIGRATION:each transition record preserves legacy version,canonical timestamp version,recorded evidence time,previous hash,entry hash and recovery evidence. SEAL:the current seal history_head must equal the latest revision and its timestamp version must equal metadata codex_version and the Chinese artifact codex_version. REGISTRIES:version_evolution_rules is legacy-retired;timestamp_version_evolution_rules is current. FAILURE:missing history,head mismatch,unproven verified recovery,non-increasing timestamp version or active numeric increment is a Codex issue and blocks a new seal without stopping unrelated runtime review.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:revision-history deletion+sequence restart+recovered evidence marked verified without proof+seal/head/version mismatch+active numeric increment+silent version migration+rewriting original legacy row.
articles.exception: A missing historical record may be represented by an explicit gap finding until evidence supports correction;inventing its content is forbidden.

articles.subject: user-authorized-history-deletion-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A413 is superseded. USER-AUTHORITY:an explicit user command to delete Codex revision history is lawful,one-time and final for the named history scope. The system,星澄,automatic repair,automatic update,checker and audit process must not restore,reconstruct,repopulate or infer deleted history. STATE:revision_history may be intentionally empty and is marked user-deleted-by-explicit-command with deletion timestamp,scope and current seal identity. CURRENT-AUTHORITY:current Codex authority is proven by the authoritative SQLite content,current timestamp version,provision identities,lineage,lifecycle,current seal roots and Chinese synchronization;deleted historical narration is not required for current operation. FUTURE:after deletion,no revision-history row is appended unless the user separately orders history recording to resume. Provision succession and seal data may continue without recreating deleted revision_history. SEPARATION:deletion does not alter current provisions,source content or external Git history.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:automatic history restoration+reconstruction from Git/mirror/cache/backup+invented recovered entries+deletion interpreted as corruption+runtime blocked solely because user-deleted history is empty+silent resumption of revision logging.
articles.exception: A separate explicit user command may authorize a new history ledger beginning after that command;it cannot recreate deleted entries without another explicit instruction.

articles.subject: active-successor-reference-and-legacy-binding-closure
articles.rule: REFERENCE-RESOLUTION:every current reference to a superseded provision resolves through provision_reference_resolution to exactly one active successor before interpretation;the predecessor remains historical identity only. A reference inside a SUCCESSOR declaration is historical evidence and is not an active dependency. CURRENT-MAP:A406 resolves to A411 for timestamp version identity;A395 resolves through A406 to A411;A397 resolves to A410 for evidence timestamps;A394 resolves to A409 for dynamic references;A398 resolves to A408 for automatic command contracts;A399 resolves to A407 for cross-Codex interpretation;A100 and A109 resolve to A412 for change classification. BINDING:legacy numeric effective_version values are preserved in legacy_effective_version while current_binding_version points to the current timestamp version;this binds existing active provisions without fabricating their original effective time. STATUS:timestamp_status uses only verified,estimated,corrected or invalid. HISTORY:revision_history remains empty under A414 and this amendment is represented by provision lineage,current seal and canonical timestamp only.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:interpreting superseded text without successor resolution+multiple active successors+rewriting historical effective version+numeric legacy field selecting current law+timestamp status outside canonical vocabulary+repopulating user-deleted revision history.
articles.exception: A deliberately historical citation may address the predecessor when explicitly marked historical and cannot control current operation.

articles.subject: typed-complete-successor-resolution-successor
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR:A415 is superseded. REGISTRY:provision_reference_resolution_v2 covers every superseded principle,article,edict and sovereign with typed predecessor identity. Each row records predecessor_type,predecessor_id,declared_successor_identity,resolved_successor_type,resolved_active_successor_id,resolution_path,status and validation timestamp. STATUS:resolved-active means the full chain terminates in exactly one active provision of the applicable type;cross-type-retirement-basis means a retired identity cites an active provision as its retirement authority rather than becoming that provision;retired-no-successor means retirement is terminal and no current semantic successor may be inferred;unresolved or cycle is incomplete evidence. INTERPRETATION:current citations automatically traverse resolved-active chains. Historical citations remain historical. A terminal retirement cannot be revived or mapped by similarity. COVERAGE:registry row count and typed predecessor set exactly equal lifecycle superseded set. FAILURE:missing row,duplicate typed predecessor,cycle,non-active resolved target or invented target blocks only the affected interpretation and produces a precise Codex finding. HISTORY:the user-deleted revision_history remains empty.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:untyped predecessor collision+partial resolution registry+invented successor+retired identity revival+cross-type retirement authority treated as identity replacement+cycle hidden+missing target treated compliant+revision history reconstruction.
articles.exception: A terminal retired identity may remain without successor when the lifecycle evidence explicitly closes it and no active rule depends on it as current authority.

articles.subject: codex-internal-modular-architecture
articles.rule: ARCHITECTURE:the Codex remains one highest-rule declaration authority and one canonical SQLite authority while its internal content is partitioned into registered non-sovereign rule modules. MODULES:foundation,authority,permission,directory,星澄,information,runtime,data,resource,language,release,external,audit,Git,learning,maintenance,test,ordinance and privacy-security each have one code,one primary responsibility and an explicit dependency boundary. MEMBERSHIP:every principle,article,edict and sovereign identity has exactly one primary module membership;cross-module citations are dependencies and never duplicate ownership. AUTHORITY:no internal module is an actor,sovereign,executor or separate law source;modules cannot decide,modify,seal or interpret independently. STORAGE:codex_internal_module_directory defines modules,codex_internal_module_membership covers every provision identity,and codex_internal_module_dependency stores a directed acyclic dependency graph. OWNER:permission-sovereign owns directory registration and validates structural coverage only;Codex remains the rule source;星澄 independently inspects module-boundary compliance. LOADING:consumers may load affected modules for bounded review but a final Codex-wide claim requires complete seal and cross-module dependency verification. FAILURE:one malformed module is isolated as incomplete evidence without silently discarding unaffected modules;no partial module may claim whole-Codex authority. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted under A414.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:multiple canonical Codex authorities+module as sovereign or executor+provision in multiple primary modules+orphan provision+implicit dependency+dependency cycle+module-local rule overriding Codex precedence+partial load presented as whole Codex+internal module stored outside canonical Codex.
articles.exception: A provision may have secondary searchable tags,which are derived indexes only and never additional ownership or authority.

articles.subject: codex-indexed-search-performance-special-law
articles.rule: SEARCH-PATH:Codex lookup resolves exact provision/code identity through indexed keys first,then narrows by codex_internal_module_membership and law classification,and uses codex_search_fts only for free-text discovery. AUTHORITY:search indexes,query caches and relevance ranking are derived,rebuildable and non-authoritative;every result rehydrates the authoritative row and verifies provision identity,lifecycle,current successor resolution,content hash,current seal and access scope before use. INDEXES:identity,lifecycle,effective status,law code,module membership,command/fault code and dependency edges have dedicated deterministic indexes. FULL-TEXT:the local SQLite FTS index covers subject and rule text with provision,module and law filters;it never enters RAG,Qdrant,external indexing or the Chinese confidential path. MODULAR:affected-module search avoids whole-Codex scans while whole-Codex review unions every registered module and proves coverage. CACHE:key includes Codex timestamp version,module set,query normalization,access scope and search-schema identity;version or policy change invalidates it. PERFORMANCE:query plans must use registered indexes for identity and bounded filtered lookups;unbounded table scans are prohibited in interactive paths. RECOVERY:missing/corrupt FTS or cache is discarded and rebuilt from authoritative SQLite rows;failure may reduce speed but never skip governance or return stale authority.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:search index as authority+RAG or external indexing of Codex+Chinese confidential content leakage+result without lifecycle/hash/seal verification+stale cache across version+relevance rank overriding precedence+interactive whole-table scan+missing module coverage presented as full review.
articles.exception: A maintenance-only full integrity scan may read all authoritative rows when explicitly requested;it remains bounded,observable and separate from interactive search.

articles.subject: codex-internal-module-manifest-and-seal
articles.rule: MANIFEST:each Codex internal module has one content-addressed manifest containing module_code,version_identity,provision_count,active_count,superseded_count,membership_hash,content_hash,dependency_hash,search_document_hash,status and sealed_at_utc. COVERAGE:the union of module memberships equals the complete provision identity set exactly once and each manifest count matches authoritative rows. SEAL:the whole-Codex seal binds the ordered module-manifest root in addition to provision and identity roots;module manifests are derived integrity evidence and never separate authority. VALIDATION:module load verifies its manifest,membership,current successor resolution and dependencies before use;whole-Codex claims verify every module and the aggregate root. UPDATE:an amendment updates affected memberships,search documents,module manifests and aggregate seal in one SQLite transaction. FAILURE:a stale/missing/mismatched module manifest isolates that module as incomplete evidence and cannot silently use its search results;unaffected modules remain reviewable. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:module without manifest+count/hash mismatch+manifest as independent authority+partial module claimed as whole Codex+non-atomic amendment/index/manifest update+stale module search accepted+history reconstruction.
articles.exception: A derived module manifest may be deterministically rebuilt from the authoritative current Codex when corruption is detected;rebuild cannot change any provision.

articles.subject: codex-search-index-freshness-and-query-plan-gate
articles.rule: SEARCH-MANIFEST:every search generation records search_schema_id,Codex version identity,authoritative content root,source_count,indexed_count,FTS tokenizer,module-manifest root,index-content hash,built_at_utc and status. FRESHNESS:a search result is usable only when manifest version and content root equal the current seal,source_count equals provision identities,indexed_count equals search documents and the source row content hash matches authoritative content. QUERY-PLAN:exact identity uses a unique index;module/law/lifecycle filters use composite indexes;short registered Chinese aliases use codex_search_alias;free text of supported length uses local FTS. The planner never converts a failed exact lookup into an unbounded scan. REBUILD:Codex amendment rebuilds changed documents and FTS atomically before sealing;corrupt or stale derived indexes are discarded and rebuilt without modifying authority. BENCHMARK:record cold/warm duration,result count,query class,plan identity and version for bounded diagnostics;performance numbers are monitoring evidence only. CONFIDENTIALITY:no Chinese mirror content,RAG,Qdrant,network or external process enters the search index.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:search without fresh manifest+source/index count drift+content-root mismatch+unindexed interactive scan+FTS as authority+stale result after amendment+external or RAG indexing+Chinese mirror ingestion+benchmark changing governance outcome.
articles.exception: A maintenance integrity scan may bypass search indexes to verify or rebuild them,while clearly marked non-interactive and non-authoritative.

articles.subject: codex-module-lifecycle-count-and-orphan-identity-closure
articles.rule: SUCCESSOR-CLARIFICATION:A419 module manifests count every lifecycle state explicitly. Each manifest contains provision_count,active_count,superseded_count,retired_count and other_state_count;their sum equals provision_count. IDENTITY-CLOSURE:every current article,principle,edict and sovereign row has exactly one provision identity,lineage row,lifecycle row,classification,module membership and search document. A lifecycle row without a provision identity is an orphan and must be removed or formally registered;retired former names that are no longer provisions cannot persist as phantom lifecycle entries. NORMALIZATION:A400 through A405 receive their missing immutable identities and lineage from their existing H092 provision revisions without altering their text. VALIDATION:zero identity/lifecycle orphans,zero module/search omissions and exact manifest totals are required before sealing. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:manifest totals excluding retired states+identity without lifecycle+lifecycle without identity+active article without lineage+phantom retired authority identity+normalization rewriting provision content+history reconstruction.
articles.exception: Unknown future lifecycle states are counted in other_state_count and make the affected manifest incomplete until their semantics are registered.

articles.subject: codex-module-and-search-manifest-complete-binding
articles.rule: MODULE-BINDING:each module manifest additionally binds lifecycle_hash,classification_hash and successor_resolution_hash for its exact member set. Counts alone are insufficient because state or classification can move between identities without changing totals. SEARCH-BINDING:the search manifest binds alias_count and alias_hash in addition to authoritative content root,document count,index hash,tokenizer and module-manifest root. Every alias target must resolve to one current search document and module membership;orphan aliases are forbidden. UPDATE:any provision,identity,lifecycle,classification,membership,successor,content or alias change invalidates affected manifests and the aggregate seal until atomically rebuilt. VALIDATION:recompute ordered hashes from authoritative tables,compare exact counts and reject stale/missing/extra rows. DERIVATION:aliases,FTS,search documents and manifests remain local,rebuildable,non-authoritative evidence and cannot alter a provision. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:count-only manifest proof+lifecycle/classification swap hidden by equal totals+successor map omitted from module seal+alias omitted from search seal+orphan alias+stale manifest accepted+derived index mutating authority+history reconstruction.
articles.exception: A module with no successor-resolution rows binds the deterministic empty-set hash rather than omitting the field.

articles.subject: codex-search-physical-index-and-dependency-dag-evidence
articles.rule: FTS-INTEGRITY:the search manifest binds both authoritative search-document hash and the independently recomputed physical FTS row hash plus exact FTS row count. Equal row counts alone do not prove parity. DAG-INTEGRITY:the module manifest generation records one aggregate dependency_graph_hash and an explicit cycle_check_status produced from the complete registered graph;per-module dependency hashes cannot replace whole-graph cycle validation. BENCHMARK-EVIDENCE:codex_search_benchmark_evidence records version identity,query class,normalized query hash,plan detail,result count,duration_microseconds,index_used,status and measured_at_utc for exact identity,module filter,short alias and FTS paths. PERFORMANCE:benchmarks are diagnostic evidence,not fixed acceptance thresholds;the required invariant is bounded indexed execution with no interactive full authoritative-table scan. FRESHNESS:any provision,module,dependency,alias,search-document or FTS change invalidates the manifest and benchmark generation until rebuilt in the same amendment transaction. AUTHORITY:all indexes and measurements remain derived and non-authoritative. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:FTS count-only proof+document hash substituted for physical FTS hash+module-local dependency hashes claimed cycle-complete+benchmark without query plan+full authoritative scan in interactive path+performance number as legal authority+stale benchmark reused across version+history reconstruction.
articles.exception: A cold-cache measurement may vary by machine and load;variance is recorded without weakening correctness or index-use requirements.

articles.subject: codex-internal-module-directory-uniform-format-successor
articles.rule: FORMAT:codex_internal_module_directory conforms to the directory common envelope in physical column order:module_code as the typed entry-code,canonical_name,directory_code,owner,scope,authority_kind,status,revision,content_hash,introduced_version,retired_version,then responsibility,authority_boundary,parent_module_code and version_identity. The former registration_owner field is normalized to owner and never duplicated. IDENTITY:module_code is the immutable uppercase entry identity and directory_code is DIR_CODEX_INTERNAL_MODULE. HASH:content_hash binds the semantic domain fields and parent relationship;revision and version_identity use the current timestamp version while introduced_version preserves first registration. RELATIONSHIPS:membership and dependency remain normalized link tables and are not delimiter-packed into the module row. VALIDATION:permission-sovereign validates common envelope,domain fields,parent resolution,membership coverage,DAG,module manifest and aggregate seal in order. MIGRATION:v1 rows transform losslessly to v2 in one transaction and the v1 format is retired. HISTORY:revision_history remains user-deleted.
articles.prohibition: FORBID:module directory without common envelope+registration_owner/owner duplication+missing content hash+packed membership/dependency text+field-order drift+unresolved parent+v1 row used after v2 activation+history reconstruction.
articles.exception: Root foundation has a null parent explicitly allowed by the v2 format contract;retired_version is null while active.

articles.subject: whole-system-recursive-modular-architecture
articles.rule: SCOPE:all GPTBridge platform-core,independent tools,information services,data adapters,model capabilities,UI,backend,workers,launchers,maintenance,tests,build and governance-support code are recursively modular. CANONICAL-TOPOLOGY:project_architecture_directory remains the sole top-level architecture authority;system_module_profile adds normalized module semantics without duplicating path or ownership truth. STRUCTURAL-NODES:project roots,containers,declaration layers and composition layers are non-runtime structural modules and cannot execute. RUNTIME-MODULES:each executable leaf has exactly one architecture_code as module_code,one identity-group binding,one lifecycle,one generation,one failure domain,one interface contract,one state owner and one execution identity. INTERNAL-MODULES:every runtime module decomposes into single-responsibility internal modules;one internal module has at most three explicitly registered capabilities and no hidden cross-module state. DEPENDENCY:system_module_dependency stores typed directed dependencies;parent containment is not execution permission;runtime calls use declared information-layer contracts. EXECUTION:top-level sovereigns decide,sub-sovereigns manage and dispatch,module-execution components alone execute. ISOLATION:failure,timeout,restart,repair,update,resource pressure and release handover are contained to the exact module and declared dependents;unaffected modules and channels continue. UI:each module publishes field-scoped state and never forces whole-UI refresh. AUTOMATION:repair/update switches,confirmation,status and executor are module-scoped;one automation failure cannot stop another. DATA:each module declares its PostgreSQL/SQLite/Qdrant ownership role and reconciliation boundary.
